reason: The only offered combination applies calcium to the fibre, advancing the goal of making it pull.

reaction: The distinction between sliding filaments and shortening filaments was useful.
reason: The only offered combination uses calcium pumps to help the fibre become ready again.

effect: Calcium pumping stopped the pull and completed the fibre goal; the next goal is to build and attach both muscles.

mostWorthwhile.text: The calcium-triggered sliding and subsequent relaxation were most worthwhile: the picture plans connect ATP, filament movement and calcium pumping without suggesting the filaments themselves shorten.

leastWorthwhile.text: The separate biceps and triceps assembly steps felt somewhat repetitive, although their different heads and attachments added useful detail.

surprise.text: Relaxation requires ATP-powered calcium pumping, and the fibre lengthens under an outside pull rather than actively pushing itself longer.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, but most were the only offered combination, so the sequence felt guided rather than discovered. 'Fascicle' was explained by the bundle label, though it initially sounded specialized.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested in seeing how the completed arm connects to further physiology, especially after the clear link between muscle attachments and movement.
